notes: This policy is the trust boundary for a patch produced by a text-only external executor. The verifier validates and describes the patch; it never applies it, never writes into the worktree, the index, the git control directory, the patch file, or any global configuration.

The lead is the only actor that may apply a patch and run its tests. A receipt from this verifier says the patch is confined and applies cleanly at exactly one strip level — it says nothing about whether the change is correct.

Enforcement authority stays split three ways and is never merged: the verifier enforces patch safety, the provider runner enforces transport and permissions, and the lead applies and tests. Passing verification grants no permission and promotes no lane.
Every rule fails closed. A shape the policy does not recognise is rejected, never ignored, and a rejected patch is not thereby proved malicious — it is a patch the lead must read by hand.

allow_flags.--allow-delete: Permits `deleted file mode` entries. Every other rule still applies unchanged: path confinement, the denied-path list, the limits, the single-strip-level rule, and the git apply check. The flag is recorded in the receipt.

denied.100755: a new file that arrives executable is a capability grant, not an edit
denied.120000: a symlink entry redirects a path outside the reviewed set
denied.160000: a gitlink entry adds a submodule and with it a second source of code

notes: `old mode`/`new mode` pairs are rejected outright: a mode change is a permission change and belongs in front of the lead, not inside a bulk patch.
An existing file that is already `100755` may be edited — the patch grants nothing that the repository did not already carry — but a `new file mode 100755` is refused.

denied_patterns.reason: the git control directory rewrites history, hooks, and configuration
gitattributes can bind a filter command and gitmodules adds a submodule
a hook directory executes on ordinary git operations
continuous-integration configuration runs code with repository credentials
direnv evaluates this file when a shell enters the directory
a shell startup file executes on the next interactive shell
private key, keystore, or encrypted secret store
the file name itself claims to hold a credential
cloud or container credentials and contexts
provider authentication or harness configuration for this kit's own executors

notes: The denied list is matched case-insensitively against the normalized path, because the filesystems this kit targets are case-insensitive and `.GIT` is `.git`.
The list is deliberately conservative and will refuse some innocent paths. A refusal is not an accusation: it means the verifier will not vouch for the patch and the lead must read it by hand.
Confinement is enforced twice — once here on the normalized path, and again by `git apply`, which is never given `--unsafe-paths`.

header_shapes.git-prefixed: every `---` side is `a/<rest>` or `/dev/null`, every `+++` side is `b/<rest>` or `/dev/null`, at least one side is a real path, and the two rests agree when both sides are real
header_shapes.unprefixed: no real `---` or `+++` side begins with `a/` or `b/`

notes: The strip level is a property of the patch text. It is fixed by the header shape before `git apply` is consulted, and never by whichever level happens to apply. Exactly two shapes are recognised — `a/<rest>` opposite `b/<rest>` means 1, no `a/` or `b/` on either side means 0 — and `/dev/null` is the missing side of an add or a delete and belongs to both.

Any other shape is refused, not guessed at. `a/x` opposite `a/x`, one side prefixed and the other bare, `b/` where `a/` belongs, or remainders that disagree do not say which component is a prefix and which is a directory: no level is established, `git apply` is never run, and the patch is rejected as `unpaired_path_prefixes`. A patch that mixes the two recognised shapes across its files is rejected as `mixed_path_prefixes`.

`require_single_applicable_level` means the patch is read at exactly one level: the one its headers fix. `git apply --check` is asked whether the patch applies there, and that answer alone decides the verdict. The other candidate is probed only to describe it in the receipt as `strip.alternate_applies`, and it is never selected — `strip.alternate_chosen` is false on every receipt this verifier prints.

For a git-prefixed patch the other candidate is `-p0`, which is not a second reading: it is the patch with its prefix left on, naming `a/…` and `b/…` paths the receipt does not list. Every ordinary add applies that way, because `b/src/x` does not exist and `--check` will create it. That reading is recorded and refused rather than counted as an alternative, so it cannot redirect the change under an extra component.

For an unprefixed patch the other candidate is `-p1`, which drops a real leading component and lands on a different existing file — and `-p1` is git's own default, so a lead can reach it by habit. A patch that also applies at `-p1` therefore has a second reading that is reachable by accident, and it is rejected as `ambiguous_strip_level`.

The unprefixed shape exists because the Qwen chat-completions lane emits `--- <path>` on both sides unless the brief demands otherwise. Recording the level in the receipt is what lets the lead apply it with the right `-p`.

environment: HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME redirected to an empty private directory
GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE and the object-directory variables unset
notes: `--check` writes nothing. It is run only after every structural and path rule has already passed, so a denied path is never handed to git at all.
git's own stderr is captured and discarded: it quotes patch context on failure and the receipt must never carry patch content.
The four digests are taken before and after the run and compared. A difference is a failure of this command, reported as exit 70, not a property of the patch.

`worktree_state_sha256` covers `status --porcelain -uall`, the unstaged diff and the staged diff, so a content change in an already-dirty file is visible. `git_control_sha256` covers HEAD, the repository config, packed refs, the ref listing, and the index digest.
Only paths, counts, operation names, rule identifiers, and digests are reported. A path that fails the character-set rule is not echoed at all — the receipt records the rule, not the bytes.

exit_codes.0: accepted: the patch is confined and applies cleanly at exactly one strip level
exit_codes.65: the patch is rejected by this policy
exit_codes.66: the patch file or worktree is missing or unreadable
exit_codes.70: the read-only attestation failed: state changed during the run
